claim.quote: Including the new results, the total exposure of DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 over 8 annual cycles is 1.53 t·yr and the evidence for a signal that meets all the requirements of the model-independent Dark Matter annual modulation signature is 11.8 σ C.L. in the energy region (1 - 6) keV.

date.quote: Nucl. Phys. At. Energy 2021, volume 22, issue 4, pages 329-342

key_value_text.quote: the achieved C.L. for the full exposure of 2.86 t·yr is 13.7 σ
key_value_text.value: the achieved C.L. for the full exposure of 2.86 t·yr is 13.7 σ

name: Further results from DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 and perspectives
notes: Source: the Tor Vergata repository record carries the abstract (it dates the item 2022); the journal issue is 22(4), 2021 according to the LNGS page and the DOI (10.15407/jnpae2021.04.329).

significance.quote: is 11.8 σ C.L. in the energy region (1 - 6) keV
significance.value: 11.8 sigma C.L. in (1-6) keV (phase2, 1.53 t yr); 13.7 sigma for the full 2.86 t yr in (2-6) keV

summary.plain: With two more years of data, DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 shows the yearly modulation at 11.8 standard deviations (eight years of data), and at 13.7 when all earlier DAMA data are included, according to the team.
summary.technical: Eight annual cycles of phase2 (1.53 t yr): 11.8 sigma in 1-6 keV; full exposure 2.86 t yr in 2-6 keV (DAMA/NaI, phase1 and phase2, 22 annual cycles): 13.7 sigma. The abstract says no systematic or side reaction mimicking the signature has been found, and mentions a preliminary result on a lower software threshold.

title: Further results from DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 and perspectives
why_it_matters: The latest published DAMA/LIBRA significance; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'. The experiment's data taking is reported to have ended in 2024 (2026 review).
